bench: m4 scale: kubernetes (shallow clone, ~32k files) alone, then linux (~97k files) added to the same store
host: 32 cores, 125 GB RAM, store on tmpfs, shared host (not quiet); treat latencies as +-2x
queries: 20 find queries scoped to kubernetes, first uncached run, process spawn included; saves are fox index re-runs after appending a function
notes: alone_top20_found_in_shared_top60 and the 'after' latencies were measured before the follow-up fixes (scope checked per match before ranking, prefix matches kept in project slices, fragmented ranges bridged into at most 8 slices, background graph rebuilds). The host was busy (load 9-24), so the 150 ms shared-store target is not shown as met on a quiet machine. Reviewer re-measurements on the same build: a 1-file save is 0.72-0.75 s no-op and about 1.0 s median on kubernetes (2-3 s for files defining very common names), and 1.64 s no-op on linux, most of it the file walk, so the single-save target holds only on kubernetes. Before the bridging fix, about 64 interleaved saves disabled project slices and search fell back to about 5.5 s; that fallback no longer exists.
